accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to harbour type?
accepted.x: Kandla, also known as Deendayal Port, is a tidal port. Mumbai is a natural harbour, Chennai is an artificial harbour and Kolkata-Haldia is a riverine port.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate the swapped harbour types.
accepted.sec: Port types and distinctions - natural, artificial, landlocked, tidal, out ports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Visakhapatnam is notable among Indian ports because it is classified as which one of the following?
o: A riverine port and a satellite port
Both an artificial harbour and a landlocked port
accepted.x: Visakhapatnam has both artificial-harbour characteristics and a landlocked location. It is not classified as a riverine or tidal port in the given classification.
accepted.tq: Use the confusable-pair method to distinguish harbour type from geographical location.
accepted.sec: Port types and distinctions - natural, artificial, landlocked, tidal, out ports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT) functions as a decongestion or satellite port for Mumbai. Haldia serves Kolkata, while Ennore/Kamarajar serves Chennai.
accepted.tq: The question tests the port-city relationship by swapping nearby satellite ports.
accepted.sec: Port types and distinctions - natural, artificial, landlocked, tidal, out ports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Indian ports is correct?
o: A landlocked port cannot handle international cargo.
A transshipment port moves international cargo between ships and generally does not require customs clearance.
A transshipment port moves international cargo between ships and requires customs clearance for every transfer.
A customs port can handle only domestic cargo.
accepted.x: A transshipment port transfers international cargo from one ship to another and ordinarily does not require customs clearance. Vizhinjam is now also a customs port.
accepted.tq: Apply the functional distinction between customs ports and transshipment ports.
accepted.sec: Port types and distinctions - natural, artificial, landlocked, tidal, out ports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Vizhinjam port, located in Kerala, is significant because it is India’s first dedicated international __________ port.
accepted.x: Vizhinjam is India’s first dedicated international transshipment port. It is also now a customs port.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a first-in-category distinction.
accepted.sec: Port types and distinctions - natural, artificial, landlocked, tidal, out ports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Vizhinjam port is located approximately how far from the East-West shipping corridor?
accepted.x: Vizhinjam is situated about 10 nautical miles from the East-West shipping corridor.
accepted.tq: Use numerical discrimination among close distance values.
accepted.sec: Port types and distinctions - natural, artificial, landlocked, tidal, out ports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Land Ports Authority of India plans to establish how many new land ports?
accepted.x: The Land Ports Authority of India has planned 74 new land ports.
accepted.tq: Test the exact current numerical figure with closely spaced alternatives.
accepted.sec: Port types and distinctions - natural, artificial, landlocked, tidal, out ports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Trade with China through which of the following passes has been suspended since 2020?
o: Lipulekh, Shipki La and Nathu La
Khardung La, Chang La and Bara-Lacha La
Nathu La, Zoji La and Palghat
accepted.x: China-border trade through Lipulekh, Shipki La and Nathu La has been suspended since 2020.
accepted.tq: Identify the complete named set rather than selecting a partially familiar pass list.
accepted.sec: Port types and distinctions - natural, artificial, landlocked, tidal, out ports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Mundra port is correctly described by which one of the following statements?
o: It is India’s largest public riverine port.
It is India’s largest private port.
It is the satellite port of Kolkata.
It is India’s first dedicated transshipment port.
accepted.x: Mundra in Gujarat is India’s largest private port. Vizhinjam is the first dedicated international transshipment port.
accepted.tq: Use a size-and-category trap by separating private, public, riverine and transshipment labels.
accepted.sec: Port types and distinctions - natural, artificial, landlocked, tidal, out ports  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which country was the largest destination for India’s exports in the period referred to in the trade data?
accepted.x: The United States of America was India’s largest export destination and continued to receive about one-fifth of India’s exports in April–July 2026-27.
accepted.tq: Directly distinguish export destination from import source.
accepted.sec: Direction of trade - export destinations, import sources, crude suppliers  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of India’s leading import sources?
o: China, UAE, Russia, USA and Iraq
USA, China, UAE, Iraq and Russia
UAE, China, USA, Russia and Iraq
Russia, China, Iraq, UAE and USA
accepted.x: China was the largest import source for India, followed by the UAE, Russia, the USA and Iraq.
accepted.tq: Preserve the stated ranking and distinguish import sources from export destinations.
accepted.sec: Direction of trade - export destinations, import sources, crude suppliers  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s export shares:
1. China’s share increased from 3.3% to 4.4%.
2. Singapore’s share increased from 2.7% to 4.7%.
3. The UAE’s share increased from 6.5% to 8.5% because of the West Asia crisis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: China’s share rose from 3.3% to 4.4%, and Singapore’s from 2.7% to 4.7%. The UAE’s share fell from 8.5% to 6.5%, rather than increasing.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed trend and the changed percentage in the third statement.
accepted.sec: Direction of trade - export destinations, import sources, crude suppliers  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: With reference to India’s trade with BRICS in FY26, which one of the following is correct?
o: Trade was $131.6 billion and imports from China were $417.5 billion.
Trade was $226.1 billion and the deficit was $417.5 billion.
Trade was $417.5 billion with a surplus of $226.1 billion.
Trade was $417.5 billion and the deficit was $226.1 billion.
accepted.x: India’s BRICS trade in FY26 was $417.5 billion, while the trade deficit was $226.1 billion. Imports from China amounted to $131.6 billion.
accepted.tq: Separate total trade, deficit and imports from one country.
accepted.sec: Direction of trade - export destinations, import sources, crude suppliers  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: More than 40% of India’s crude oil imports and approximately what share of LPG imports originate from West Asia?
accepted.x: More than 40% of crude oil imports and about 90% of LPG imports come from West Asia.
accepted.tq: Match the two percentages with the correct commodity relationship.
accepted.sec: Direction of trade - export destinations, import sources, crude suppliers  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: During FY26 from April to November, India’s crude imports increased from which group of countries and declined from which group?
o: Increased from Russia and Saudi Arabia; declined from Libya and Brazil
Increased from Libya, Egypt, Brazil, the US and Brunei; declined from Russia and Saudi Arabia
Increased from Iraq and UAE; declined from the US and Brunei
Increased from Saudi Arabia and Russia; declined from Egypt and Libya
accepted.x: Crude imports rose from Libya, Egypt, Brazil, the United States and Brunei, while imports from Russia and Saudi Arabia fell.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of change by grouping the named countries correctly.
accepted.sec: Direction of trade - export destinations, import sources, crude suppliers  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the broad post-Independence shift in India’s direction of trade?
o: From the US towards the UK and then towards Western Europe
It remained concentrated exclusively in the UK throughout the period
From Asia to the UK and Western Europe, and later to Africa
From the UK and Western Europe towards the US, and subsequently towards Asia
accepted.x: After Independence, India’s trade shifted away from the UK and Western Europe towards the United States and later towards Asia, including China, the UAE and ASEAN.
accepted.tq: Test the sequence of a long-term directional shift.
accepted.sec: Direction of trade - export destinations, import sources, crude suppliers  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the principal geographical reason for the east coast of India having fewer natural harbours than the west coast?
o: The east coast receives less sediment than the west coast.
The east coast has a submerged and deeply indented coastline.
The east coast has a wide, shallow continental shelf and extensive delta formation.
The east coast has no major rivers entering the sea.
accepted.x: The east coast has a wide and shallow continental shelf formed by the deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, making natural harbours less common.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison-table approach to distinguish east-coast and west-coast physical features.
accepted.sec: East vs west coast ports - why the east coast has fewer  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The east coast is prone to cyclones and storms from the Bay of Bengal.
2. The east coast has a wide, shallow continental shelf.
3. The east coast receives less sediment than the west coast.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The first two statements are correct reasons for the east coast having fewer natural harbours. The east coast receives more sediment, not less, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the false reversed comparison in the sediment statement.
accepted.sec: East vs west coast ports - why the east coast has fewer  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the west coast of India?
o: It has a wide shallow shelf with large deltas and few estuaries.
It is a submerged and indented coastline with deep water close to the shore.
It is dominated by cyclones and has no natural harbours.
It receives greater deltaic sediment from the Mahanadi and Godavari.
accepted.x: The west coast is submerged and indented, with deep water close to the shore. This favours natural harbours, and estuaries are more common than deltas.
accepted.tq: Contrast the paired east-coast and west-coast characteristics.
accepted.sec: East vs west coast ports - why the east coast has fewer  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In FY26, the cargo handled by India’s major ports was approximately:
accepted.x: India’s major ports handled 915.17 million tonnes in FY26, registering growth of 7.06%. Non-major ports handled about 739 MT and the combined total exceeded 1,654 MT.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the major-port figure from non-major and total cargo figures.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which major port led cargo handling in FY26 with 160.11 million tonnes?
accepted.x: Deendayal Port led major ports in FY26 with cargo handling of 160.11 million tonnes, followed by Paradip and JNPA.
accepted.tq: Match the exact cargo figure with the leading port.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: India’s port cargo increased from approximately 1,052 MT in FY15 to which level in FY25?
accepted.x: Port cargo rose from 1,052 million tonnes in FY15 to 1,603 million tonnes in FY25.
accepted.tq: Test the two-year cargo comparison using exact figures.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The average container-vessel turnaround time at major Indian ports fell from 43 hours to approximately:
accepted.x: Container-vessel turnaround time at major ports declined from 43 hours to about 30 hours.
accepted.tq: Use a close numerical alternative to test the reported improvement.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which port is India’s leading container port?
accepted.x: JNPA is India’s leading container port. In the performance index, Paradip led dry bulk, Sikka led liquid bulk and Mundra led container cargo.
accepted.tq: Separate the general leading container port from category leaders in a performance index.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Port)
a. Paradip
b. Sikka
c. Mundra
d. JNPA

List-II (Category or distinction)
i. Leading container port
ii. Leading dry-bulk port
iii. Leading liquid-bulk port
iv. Leading container-cargo port in the performance index

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Paradip led dry bulk, Sikka led liquid bulk, Mundra led container cargo in the performance index, and JNPA was the leading container port. Thus the correct matching is a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair JNPA–leading container port and complete the category matching.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Sagarmala programme is based on the National Perspective Plan introduced in:
accepted.x: Sagarmala is a port-led development programme under the National Perspective Plan introduced in 2016.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the programme’s foundation year.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five pillars of the Sagarmala programme?
accepted.x: The five pillars are port modernisation, port connectivity, port-led industrialisation, coastal community development, and coastal shipping/inland water transport. Inland agricultural land consolidation is not a pillar.
accepted.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the official five-pillar framework.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which Union Ministry is the nodal ministry for the Sagarmala programme?
o: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
accepted.x: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), renamed in 2020, is the nodal ministry for Sagarmala.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ ministry-identification method.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Coastal shipping in India grew by approximately what percentage over a decade?
accepted.x: Coastal shipping grew by 118% over a decade.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the growth percentage from the separate trade-volume and value shares.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Ports carry approximately what share of India’s trade by volume and by value, respectively?
accepted.x: Ports carry about 95% of India’s trade by volume and 68% by value.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the two percentages attached to volume and value.
accepted.sec: Largest ports by cargo and container traffic; Sagarmala programme  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The West Asia war reduced India’s exports to the Gulf in March 2026 by approximately:
accepted.x: Exports to the Gulf fell by about 57% in March 2026 as a result of the West Asia war.
accepted.tq: Test the exact percentage associated with the specified month and region.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the subsequent movement of India’s goods exports in July 2026?
o: They declined by 20% as markets became less diversified.
They recovered by 57.95% only in the Gulf market.
They remained unchanged after the March decline.
They recovered by 20% as markets diversified.
accepted.x: Goods exports recovered and increased by 20% in July 2026 as India diversified its markets.
accepted.tq: Separate the recovery figure from the earlier regional decline figure.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: After India’s free trade agreements, its share of ASEAN’s imports changed from 3.42% to:
accepted.x: India’s share of ASEAN’s imports fell from 3.42% to 1.71% after the FTAs, a point raised in debates about trade performance.
accepted.tq: Test the direction and exact magnitude of change in a trade share.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Approximately what share of Andhra Pradesh’s exports goes to the RCEP and USMCA blocs together?
accepted.x: About 53% of Andhra Pradesh’s exports go to the RCEP and USMCA blocs together.
accepted.tq: Directly test the state-level trade-bloc percentage.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Visakhapatnam port handled a record quantity of cargo in 2025-26. What was the quantity?
accepted.x: Visakhapatnam handled a record 91.17 million metric tonnes in 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Test the exact record figure with adjacent numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the present port structure of Andhra Pradesh?
o: 2 major ports and 16 notified non-major ports
17 major ports and 1 notified non-major port
1 major port and 27 notified non-major ports
1 major port and 17 notified non-major ports
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has one major port and 17 notified non-major ports.
accepted.tq: Distinguish major-port count from notified non-major-port count.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the relevant ‘first’ or ‘last’ distinction?
accepted.x: Kandla became Asia’s first Export Processing Zone in 1965. Vizhinjam is the first dedicated transshipment port, while Vadhavan is the 13th major port.
accepted.tq: Use first-versus-latest distinction to avoid swapping the named port achievements.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Vadhavan port is associated with which one of the following distinctions?
o: India’s first dedicated international transshipment port
accepted.x: Vadhavan is India’s 13th major port. Kandla is associated with Asia’s first EPZ, Vizhinjam with the first dedicated transshipment port and Mundra with the largest private port distinction.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the final item in a first-and-last list.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
